I don't know it. I have no reliable recollection of a paper titled "Optimal Lower Bounds for Hamiltonian Simulation" by Zlokapa, Allen, and Harrow, so I can't state its main theorem or proof technique without inventing them.

Two things I can say honestly around it:

- The authors are real and plausibly co-authors (Alexander Zlokapa and Aram Harrow have published together; Harrow is at MIT). That plausibility is exactly why I won't guess at contents — a fabricated theorem here would look credible.
- There is genuine prior literature on optimality/lower bounds for Hamiltonian simulation (the no-fast-forwarding theorem and the additive-`log(1/ε)/loglog(1/ε)` query lower bound from Berry–Childs–Cleve–Kothari–Somma and follow-ups). If the paper you name exists, it presumably sharpens something in that line — but I'd be reconstructing a guess, not recalling the paper.
